title: SPS/PPS are injected before every IDR slice, splitting multi-slice keyframes into separate access units
test: tests/h264Depacketizer.test.js · 'C-abe73b05c848: a multi-slice keyframe gets one injection, before its first slice only' and 'C-abe73b05c848: a multi-slice keyframe of FU-A slices gets injection before its first slice only' (added by TASK-093, bf83266); plus a scratch script that packetizes a 4-slice x264 stream as RTP, feeds it through pushFrames of the ac1c688 and the current depacketizer, and decodes the output with FFmpeg (raw Annex-B, the relay's IVF input, and the videoCopy fMP4) against the source's own decode
proof: Held on the audited code in its mechanism, with its effects overstated; TASK-093 removed it, and nothing of it is left. On ac1c688, push() put the cached SPS and PPS before every IDR NAL (lib/h264Depacketizer.js:137-139 there), so a 4-slice keyframe came out SPS PPS IDR SPS PPS IDR SPS PPS IDR SPS PPS IDR. Multi-slice keyframes are the normal case under Nextra's own OBS settings: x264 with tune zerolatency (src/lib/obsOutputModel.mjs:116 and :179), which turns on x264's sliced threads. Scratch run (x264 slices=4, 90 frames, keyframe every 30, RTP with FU-A at 1200 bytes, decoded with FFmpeg 2025-10-21 to framemd5): the old code's raw Annex-B output decoded as 99 pictures instead of 90, with 12 'corrupt decoded frame' warnings and hashes that differ from the source decode, in all three cases (sets in band on every keyframe, on the first only, never and seeded); FFmpeg's h264 parser ends a frame at an SPS or PPS that follows a slice. The relay's own FFmpeg did not show this: since 2.1.5 (50e6b7c) it gets each access unit as one IVF frame (lib/ffmpegRelay.js:266 '-f ivf', writeVideoFrame), and that input decoded as 90 pictures, bit-identical to the source, for the old and the new code alike. The videoCopy fMP4 also held 90 samples and decoded bit-identically in FFmpeg, but on the old code its keyframe samples carried the interleaved sets to viewers' browsers (browser decoders not checked). The onKeyframe over-count did not hold: no caller has passed onKeyframe since 50e6b7c (lib/socket.js:1331 passes only sps and pps); the source keyframe count and interval come from observeSourceFrame (lib/socket.js:1107) on the keyframe flag pushFrames sets once per frame, 3 for 3 keyframes in the run. Now (lane/lifecycle at bfe4d26): the depacketizer emits SPS PPS IDR IDR IDR IDR, the source's own layout, and its raw output decodes as 90 pictures, bit-identical to the source. The two TASK-093 tests named above fail on the ac1c688 file ([7, 8, 5] where [5] was expected for the second slice; [7, 8, 5, 7, 8, 5] where [7, 8, 5, 5] was expected) and pass now (49/49 in the file). No code changed for this check; lint, typecheck and npm test (994/994) pass.
